summary.text: 3 of 3 hidden signals for McDonald's have fresh data: 1 tailwind, 1 headwind, 0 neutral, 1 context. The biggest mover is “Egg prices (breakfast costs)” (-39.8% vs the same period last year). These are clues, not forecasts.

ai.text: Recent economic data hints that McDonald's could be facing mixed cost pressures right now. While higher ground beef prices suggest a mild headwind, plummeting egg prices act as a notable tailwind that eases breakfast costs. Meanwhile, the rising price of eating out provides broader context as restaurant prices climb faster overall.

signals.name: Ground beef prices
signals.metric: Average U.S. price of 100% ground beef per pound (BLS, monthly)
signals.what: What a pound of ground beef costs at retail, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
signals.why: Beef is the core of the menu. Rising beef costs squeeze margins for McDonald's and its franchisees unless they raise prices.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.basis: vs the same period last year
signals.now: Average U.S. price of 100% ground beef per pound (BLS, monthly): $6.88/lb (last 3 months, average), up 10% vs the same period last year. Data through Aug 2026. In plain English: beef is pricier than a year ago, a cost headwind. We read that as a mild headwind for McDonald's.

signals.name: Price of eating out
signals.metric: Consumer price index for food away from home (monthly, BLS)
signals.what: How fast restaurant prices are rising across the U.S., from the consumer price index.
signals.why: Rising menu prices lift revenue per order, but when eating out gets too expensive, budget diners cut back. That is why we treat it as context.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.basis: vs the same period last year
signals.now: Consumer price index for food away from home (monthly, BLS): 396.8 (last 3 months, average), up 3.4% vs the same period last year. Data through Aug 2026. In plain English: restaurant prices are rising faster. For McDonald's the effect cuts both ways, so we show it as context, not a call.

signals.name: Egg prices (breakfast costs)
signals.metric: Average U.S. price of a dozen large Grade A eggs (BLS, monthly)
signals.what: What a dozen eggs costs on average, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
signals.why: Breakfast is a big, high-margin daypart, and the Egg McMuffin runs on eggs. Egg spikes have squeezed restaurant costs before.

source.name: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

signals.basis: vs the same period last year
signals.now: Average U.S. price of a dozen large Grade A eggs (BLS, monthly): $2.20/dozen (last 3 months, average), down 40% vs the same period last year. Data through Aug 2026. In plain English: eggs are cheaper than a year ago, easing breakfast costs. We read that as a notable tailwind for McDonald's.
